scope: Linux desktop guidance is toolkit- and desktop-specific. GNOME HIG targets GTK4 and Libadwaita; Buoy uses GTK4 and does not imply Libadwaita. KDE HIG describes another design system.

rules.title: Use the Linux primary modifier for standard editing
rules.applicability: GTK apps following GNOME shortcut conventions
rules.guidance: Standard editing actions use Ctrl-based shortcuts. Review copied macOS Command modifiers or system-reserved Super modifiers.
exceptions: Intentional application-specific alternate bindings are advisory and suppressible.
This does not prove a command callback works or require every action to have a shortcut.

rules.title: Keyboard operation of splitter handles
rules.guidance: GTK exposes keyboard actions for focusing, moving, accepting and cancelling divider movement. Verify the actual Buoy control remains operable through these paths.
exceptions: Initial geometry and native widget type do not prove keyboard access.
No probe is unverified; only a matching failed probe produces a warning.

rules.title: Large-text and high-contrast operation
rules.guidance: Exercise the interface with enlarged text and high-contrast styling. Verify readable content and usable controls rather than accepting one default-theme screenshot.
exceptions: No theme or font setting is changed by linting.
Missing mode probes stay unverified; failed source-matched probes warn.

rules.title: Descriptive accessible names
rules.guidance: Standard widgets provide accessibility defaults; supply application-specific names when these are incomplete. Custom widgets need appropriate role, state and action exposure.
exceptions: Do not require redundant explicit names when the natural caption is meaningful.
A nonempty value is not necessarily a meaningful field label.

rules.title: Real label relationships and mnemonics
rules.applicability: GTK text labels and associated controls
rules.guidance: Inspect native labelled-by relationships and mnemonic targets when testing a visual label/control pair. Physical proximity alone cannot establish the association.
exceptions: Requires native relation observations not present in the basic PreviewKit snapshot.
Do not set GTK-managed inverse relations directly.

rules.title: Complete keyboard navigation and visible focus
rules.guidance: Verify Tab and reverse-Tab navigation, activation and visible focus across the full interface. A focusable property alone is insufficient evidence.
exceptions: Arrow-key navigation inside composite widgets may be correct.
Read-only or decorative content need not be a Tab stop.

rules.title: Context-sensitive tooltip coverage
rules.applicability: GNOME primary-window header bars; other controls only where useful
rules.guidance: Header-bar controls should have explanatory tooltips. Elsewhere, provide them selectively and do not rely on hover text for essential instructions.
exceptions: This is not a blanket requirement for every GTK or KDE control.
NativeTooltip attachment and header-bar membership need runtime metadata.
AccessibleHint and a hover tooltip are distinct surfaces.

rules.title: GNOME primary-menu conventions
rules.applicability: Apps explicitly adopting GNOME primary-menu design
rules.guidance: GNOME commonly uses primary, secondary and context menus. Primary menus include About and may include Preferences, Keyboard Shortcuts and Help. They omit Close/Quit entries.
exceptions: Do not demand a Windows-style File/Edit menu bar for all Linux apps.
Conventional menu-bar applications and KDE applications use different patterns.
Localized captions and menu purpose require explicit policy.

rules.title: Default action and cancellation semantics
rules.applicability: GTK dialogs and dialog-like application windows
rules.guidance: A default widget handles Enter. Validate cancellation through actual keyboard behavior instead of the presence of a Cancel label.
exceptions: GtkDialog has an Escape close binding but is deprecated since GTK 4.10.
A Buoy Window is not necessarily a GtkDialog; do not assume that default binding.
Destructive actions can intentionally lack a default.

rules.title: Spacing uses the selected toolkit/design system
rules.applicability: Project-selected GTK/GNOME or KDE/Kirigami design policy
rules.guidance: KDE recommends symbolic Kirigami spacing and size units. Keep platform profiles explicit; do not turn these values into universal fixed-pixel GTK rules.
exceptions: Buoy uses GTK4 on Linux, not Kirigami.
Theme, font scale and toolkit units affect physical dimensions.
Use configured relational spacing; optical adjustments remain advisory.

rules.title: Adaptive layout across window sizes
rules.applicability: GNOME applications; useful broader GTK validation
rules.guidance: Test constrained and expanded window sizes while preserving usable functionality. Sidebar proportions, clipping and disrupted grouping need multiple native captures.
exceptions: GNOME-specific target sizes are not universal Linux requirements.
An initial source frame does not prove resize behavior.

rules.title: System typography and scalable text
rules.applicability: GTK apps following GNOME typography guidance
rules.guidance: Prefer system-provided typography and avoid absolute font choices that defeat accessibility scaling. Validate custom typography rather than treating every explicit font as an error.
exceptions: Branded content, editors and specialized document rendering may require custom fonts.
A fixed source size alone does not prove scaling is broken.

rules.title: Orca screen-reader task audit
rules.applicability: AT-SPI applications, including GTK and KDE
rules.guidance: Perform tasks using a screen reader and keyboard; inspect whether controls are intelligible and distinguishable, and whether essential information survives without vision.
exceptions: An accessibility tree snapshot is necessary evidence, not proof of a successful user task.
Repeated names can be valid in distinct contextual groups.

probeContract.scope: The parent linter validates the preview source hash. Each record may specify root and platform; wrong scopes are ignored.
probeContract.producerStatus: The rule module consumes supplied probe evidence; it does not itself drive these interactions.
